chapter: Barnet, 52nd Street and New York recording dates
title: Tunes and arrangements on the Rubberlegs date
summary: Young sang four vocals; Clyde Hart arranged, and Hart died of TB not long after.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: According to the list I have of that same personnel, you did four vocals, right, 'Dream of You,' 'Seventh Avenue,' 'Sorta Kinda' and 'Ooh-ooh, my-my, oh-oh'?

Yeah, that's right. That's right. I don't know who wrote. I wrote one of those tunes, 'Sorta Kinda,' and I think 'Seventh Avenue,' Specs Powell wrote that. 'Dream of You,' Sy Oliver wrote that; but I don't know who did that 'Ooh-ooh, My-my, Oh-oh,' but Clyde made all the arrangements. I do know that, Clyde Hart.
And this is -- was not too long before Clyde died.
He had TB, you know. And I used to --
Yeah, probably. I don't remember the year for that, but we were doing an awful lot of recordings around there at that particular time, you know.
